summary: This note covers the French and Indian War (1754–1763), the North American theater of the Seven Years' War between British America and New France, with Native American allies on both sides. It describes the war's outcome in the Treaty of Paris, including France's cessions of territory to Britain and Spain, and the Royal Proclamation of 1763 that followed. It also covers the war's naming, the lead-up through the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, the 1760 Montreal capitulation, the Battle of Carillon, and the Albany Congress of 1754.
one_line: Overview of the French and Indian War (1754–1763), the North American theater of the Seven Years' War, its causes, outcome, and names.
key_facts: The French and Indian War (1754–1763) was the North American theater of the worldwide Seven Years' War.
At the start of the war, French North American colonies had roughly 60,000 settlers, compared with 2 million in the British North American colonies.
The European nations declared war on one another in 1756, escalating the war into an intercontinental conflict.
The Treaty of Paris was signed on 10 February 1763, and the Treaty of Hubertusburg settled the European theater on 15 February 1763.
France chose to cede its continental North American possessions east of the Mississippi rather than Guadeloupe and Martinique, and kept Saint Pierre and Miquelon.
France ceded French Louisiana, including New Orleans, to its ally Spain as compensation for Spain's loss of Florida to Britain.
Spain had ceded Florida to Britain in exchange for the return of Havana, Cuba.
King George III issued the Royal Proclamation of 1763 on October 7, 1763, reserving lands west of the Appalachian Mountains for Indians.
The Quebec Act of 1774 maintained French Civil law, including the seigneurial system.
In September 1760, Governor Vaudreuil negotiated a capitulation with General Amherst that let French residents keep their Roman Catholic worship and property.
At the Battle of Carillon, about 3,600 Frenchmen defeated Abercrombie's force of 18,000 regulars, militia and Native American allies.
John Bradstreet destroyed Fort Frontenac on an expedition ordered by Abercrombie.
The Albany Congress convened in June and July 1754 to formalize a unified front in dealings with Indians.
The name French and Indian War is used mainly in the United States, and the war was also called the Fourth Intercolonial War and the Great War for the Empire.
The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle in 1748 ended the War of the Austrian Succession without resolving North American territorial disputes.

entities.name: French and Indian War
entities.role: The North American theater of the Seven Years' War, fought 1754–1763 between British America and New France.

entities.name: Seven Years' War
entities.role: Worldwide conflict of which the French and Indian War was the North American theater; declared in Europe in 1756.

entities.name: Royal Proclamation of 1763
entities.role: Decree issued by King George III on October 7, 1763, dividing and administering the newly conquered territory and reserving lands west of the Appalachians for Indians.

entities.name: King George III
entities.role: British monarch who issued the Royal Proclamation of 1763.

entities.name: Quebec Act
entities.role: 1774 act that made accommodations for Roman Catholic Canadians and maintained French Civil law and the seigneurial system.

entities.name: Treaty of Paris
entities.role: Treaty signed on 10 February 1763 that officially ended the North American war.

entities.name: Treaty of Hubertusburg
entities.role: Treaty signed on 15 February 1763 that settled the European theater of the Seven Years' War.

entities.name: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle
entities.role: 1748 treaty that formally ended the War of the Austrian Succession and left North American disputes unresolved.

entities.name: Voltaire
entities.role: French philosopher who referred to Canada disparagingly as nothing more than a few acres of snow.

entities.name: Governor Vaudreuil
entities.role: Governor who negotiated a capitulation with General Amherst from Montreal in September 1760.

entities.name: General Amherst
entities.role: British general who granted Vaudreuil's capitulation request in September 1760.

entities.name: Jeffery Amherst
entities.role: Victor at Louisbourg who replaced Abercrombie as commander.

entities.name: Abercrombie
entities.role: British commander whose force of 18,000 was defeated at the Battle of Carillon.

entities.name: John Bradstreet
entities.role: Officer who destroyed Fort Frontenac on an expedition sent by Abercrombie.

entities.name: Battle of Carillon
entities.role: Battle in which 3,600 Frenchmen defeated Abercrombie's force outside the fort the French called Carillon and the British called Ticonderoga.

entities.name: Fort Frontenac
entities.role: Fort destroyed by John Bradstreet's expedition, including supply caches for New France's western forts.

entities.name: Albany Congress
entities.role: Meeting held in June and July 1754 to formalize a unified front in trade and negotiations with Indians.

entities.name: Battle of Jumonville Glen
entities.role: 1754 battle that marked the start of the fighting on mainland North America.

entities.name: Saint Pierre and Miquelon
entities.role: Two small islands in the Gulf of St. Lawrence that France retained after the war.

entities.name: Louisiana
entities.role: French territory west of the Mississippi, including New Orleans, ceded to Spain.

entities.name: Havana
entities.role: Cuban city returned to Spain in exchange for Florida.

entities.name: Iroquois
entities.role: Native American nation that supported the British colonists at various times.

entities.name: Abenaki
entities.role: Wabanaki Confederacy member that supported the French colonists.
